To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the efficiency of transfection of cells by the use(s) of synthetic amphiphile(s) is dependent on the size of the vesicle, the size of the plasmid DNA, the lipid/DNA ratio and the toxicity of the carrier system.
transfection efficiency is affected by the amphiphile concentration and the size of the complexed DNA.
optimal transfection by DOTMA is obtained at low amphiphile concentrations, that the translocation process is dependent on the size of the vesicle and DNA, and is inhibited by Ca2+.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of carriers for the delivery of nucleic acids to cells, and with the elucidation of the mechanism of transfection.
the development of synthetic amphiphile-based carriers for DNA translocation into cells, with the aim of optimizing the carrier system for the introduction of DNA into cells.

the elucidation of the mechanism of transfection of cells with DNA by the use of cationic amphipathic lipids as a carrier system, in particular with the aim to identify the parameters that influence the efficiency of this transfection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the translocation of DNA into cells via carriers composed of synthetic amphiphile can be achieved in a highly efficient way by using DOTMA, and that the mechanism of translocation involves formation of pores in the cell membrane, possibly mediated by a Ca2+ sensitive protein.

the mechanism of translocation of DNA via synthetic amphiphiles involves a combination of factors, including the size and charge of the complex, its interaction with the cell membrane, and the properties of the membrane itself.
the mechanism of transfection by synthetic amphiphiles is not well understood, and that further studies on the mechanism are needed to optimize the properties of the amphiphile carriers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the efficiency of transfection is determined by the balance between the efficiency of interaction of the DNA/amphilphile complex with the target cell surface and the toxicity of the complex towards the cells.

the transfection efficiency is determined by the balance of several parameters: the lipid/DNA ratio in the complex, the size of the vesicles and DNA, the time of incubation, and the toxicity of the lipid towards the cell.
the transfection efficiency depends on a delicate balance between the concentration of the amphiphile, the lipid/DNA ratio, the size of the vesicles, the size of DNA and the time of incubation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the efficiency of DNA translocation is determined by the ability of the amphiphile to form pores across the membrane and by the toxicity of the complex.
the efficiency of the DNA translocation is dependent on the interaction of the vesicles with the cell surface.
the mechanism of DNA uptake by the cells is dependent on the amphiphile concentration.
